pipelines.title: Problem lookup
pipelines.line: Search the stored problems before spending tokens on solving one.

pipelines.title: Reasoning cache
pipelines.line: A cheaper model reuses solutions that a stronger model produced.

pipelines.title: Code queries
pipelines.line: An agent sends a query and gets a few hundred tokens back instead of whole files.

pipelines.title: Graph model training
pipelines.line: Learn from past commits which files are related; runs on the GPU.

pipelines.title: Code map
pipelines.line: Scripts turn the repository into a graph of facts; no model is used.

pipelines.title: Problem records
pipelines.line: The session that solves a hard problem records it, with a check that proves the cause.

pipelines.title: Standing notes
pipelines.line: Text loaded into every session at start.

pipelines.title: Library
pipelines.line: The project's record of decisions, measurements and mistakes.

pipelines.title: Plan
pipelines.line: Split a request into units of work and order them.

pipelines.title: Admit
pipelines.line: Decide which units start now, and on which model.

pipelines.title: Work
pipelines.line: Units run as a tree of sessions, one purpose per session.

pipelines.title: Check
pipelines.line: Test and review every change before it is merged.

pipelines.title: Land
pipelines.line: Merge checked changes one at a time, in order.

pipelines.title: Learn
pipelines.line: Record the measurements and findings of the task.

pipelines.title: Guards
pipelines.line: Scripts that check a step before it runs and can refuse it.

pipelines.title: Limits
pipelines.line: The number of units that run at once is set by the tightest limit.

pipelines.title: Context
pipelines.line: Keep each session's context window small, since every call re-reads all of it.

pipelines.title: Recovery
pipelines.line: Work is kept and resumed when a session or the machine fails.

pipelines.title: Measurement and research
pipelines.line: Measurements and research are used to revise the harness rules.

enforcers.what: At every start, resume, clear and compaction, puts the board's look-up table and next task into the context and says to read the board first.
enforcers.logsExcept: Its lines carry no session id: tie them to sessions by start time
enforcers.cannotSee: Whether the board or any record is then read. Its log lines carry no session id, so they can be tied to a session only by time. If the look-up table grows past about 9,000 characters its last rows are cut.

enforcers.what: Refuses a helper or child session whose description or title does not start with a known kind of job, that passes no model, or whose model the route for that kind does not allow; refuses a child session in a folder whose settings do not name the tier hook.
enforcers.logsExcept: Calls to other tools are not checked and leave no line; an input it cannot read leaves a line with no session and no tool (none so far)
enforcers.cannotSee: A job given the wrong kind; the effort level; whether an orchestrator's children have children; a child session offered as a card or started from an approved proposal (passed unchecked); helpers a workflow script starts (not probed); the session's own model. A crash or timeout lets the call through.

enforcers.what: Refuses a change, rename or removal of archived evidence; any write to the journal except through the journal tool, appends and shell forms included; git commands that would drop uncommitted journal lines; a question to the owner not starting approve:, cap: or fact:.
enforcers.cannotSee: A path computed inside a script file, or held in a variable in a command that does not name the journal; the two manifest files themselves; git commit with --no-verify; a question asked in plain text, or a design question given an allowed label; writes by tools outside its matcher. A crash lets the call through.

enforcers.what: While the build's plan file exists, refuses a helper start or revival that names a planned unit when its kind or model differs from the plan, a unit it depends on is not done, a helper for the same unit and role still runs, or its batch is full. Logs every start, run and end.
enforcers.cannotSee: Every start that names no unit of its one plan, which is the finished build of 2026-11-19, so today's work passes untouched; child sessions (start_session is not matched). A crash lets the call through.

enforcers.what: Reads the context of the last call from the transcript. Past a warning line it adds a notice; past the hard line it refuses every call except the hand-over ones (state, brief and result files, git and journal-tool commands, closing box, successor session, a stop message to a helper, a question to the owner).
enforcers.logsExcept: Every call, inside helpers too; an input it cannot read leaves a line with no session (1 so far); test-on and test-off lines (field ev) are not checks
enforcers.cannotSee: Anything below the warning line; a coordinator not named in a state file gets the looser checkpoint line; a helper whose transcript is not found passes; a model whose window is unknown gets no compaction cap; the transcript lags the live call by about 5 K. A crash lets the call through.

enforcers.what: Counts the helpers running now in the session, helpers of helpers included, and refuses a start, or a message that would revive an ended helper, past the app's limit of 20 or past a width or hold a plan declared in the widths file (none declared today).
enforcers.logsExcept: A SendMessage gets a line only when it would revive an ended helper
enforcers.cannotSee: Memory, processor, token windows and the parent's window; child sessions; heavy shell commands; whether a declared width was computed. With no width declared it refuses only what the app itself would. An error lets the start through.

enforcers.what: Refuses a helper start whose stated token limit has no expected figure, is not above it, or cites no existing measured or observed record; under a cap in the session's state file, one with no limit or whose limits pass the cap; and any start with no usage reading in an earlier message, after the last wave, under 26 minutes old and under a meter line the state file sets.
enforcers.logsExcept: Only a hook input it cannot read. Its first three lines (2026-11-23 19:29-19:32Z, session 6d4e3fd7, no tu) are hand runs that answer no call: not seen
enforcers.cannotSee: Child sessions (start_session is not matched); a start with no limit where no cap is set; whether the cited record fits the work; the coordinator's own tokens; the owner's own use since the reading; if the caller's transcript is not found the meter is not checked. An error lets the start through.

enforcers.what: Refuses record ids, unit names, repository paths, money and 'in no paper' in the closing box, in a page published through Artifact, and in a top session's last message (asked once; the next stop passes). Counts figures in the closing box as a note only.
enforcers.logsExcept: An Artifact call whose action is not publish; a helper's stop. A top session's stop gets a line. About 1,900 of its first 2,000 lines carry no session (replays or tests, inferred): skip them
enforcers.cannotSee: Whether the picture comes first, the words are plain or the text short; how many figures (a note only); a second stop; a page opened as a file and never published; a helper's return; text a script draws on a page. A crash lets the call through.

enforcers.what: After each shell call, compares every journal file with the state the journal tool last wrote, or the last commit; a file changed by another route is reported to the session once. It runs after the call and cannot undo it.
enforcers.cannotSee: Writes by tools other than the shell (left to the record guard); it cannot undo a change. No log line exists yet, so its session field is read from the code only. A crash lets the session go on.

enforcers.what: Refuses a commit that changes, renames or deletes archived evidence or a journal file, changes or drops a journal line, adds a malformed record or a line the journal tool did not write, or loses a line the tool appended since the last commit.
enforcers.cannotSee: git commit with --no-verify; merges without conflicts, cherry-picks and rebases (git runs no pre-commit hook); a clone without the hooks path set; whether a record's content or status is true; work never committed.

enforcers.what: The only way to add records: numbers them, checks them by the commit check's rules, and appends under a lock; refuses invalid records and a journal file not in the state it last wrote. Sessions run it; the record guard leaves no other route.
enforcers.cannotSee: Nothing forces a session to call it except the record guard and the commit check; whether a record is true.

enforcers.what: Turns the 13 archived FixFlow skills off and denies the 12 FixFlow agent types; the app is to refuse those calls (not checked here).
enforcers.cannotSee: A skill or agent copied under another name; any new skill, agent or always-loaded file. Nothing is logged.
